लपिता: Lapitā f.: A female Śārṅgikā bird. The great sage Mandapāla, turned into a शार्ङ्गक bird, first approached the Śārṅ-gikā Jaritā, but later transferred his attention to Lapitā 1. 220. 17; at the time of the Khāṇḍava fire, when Mandapāla expressed his anxiety about the safety of his young ones, Lapitā became jealous and said that Mandapāla was not really anxious for his young sons but for Jaritā, his first love; she knew that his children were powerful, lustrous, and able speakers; they need have no fear from fire; moreover Mandapāla had in her presence secured an assurance from god Agni that he would not harm Manda-pāla's children; Lapitā therefore was sure that Mandapāla was really worried about Jaritā, her foe; she charged Mandapāla that he did not love her as he loved Jaritā and asked him to go to Jaritā and leave her alone 1. 224. 2-13.
लोमश: Lomaśa m.: A cat. A. Residence: He lived on the branches of a banyan tree in a certain forest 12. 136. 19, 22; also in a hole (स्वबिलम्) at the foot of the tree 12. 136. 190. B. Description: Had sharp front teeth and eyes resembling the cat's-eye gem; he was intelligent, eloquent (वाक्यसंपन्न) and knew the import of speech वाक्यतत्त्वज्ञ) 12. 136. 65, 64, 94. C. Palita-Lomaśa Episode: A mouse, Palita, also lived in a hole at the foot of the banyan tree; Lomaśa, although normally watchful (अप्रमत्त 12. 136. 25), was once caught in a trap (उन्माथ 12. 136. 23) fixed by a Cāṇḍāla; when this happened Palita began to move about freely, got a piece of flesh, and started eating it on the top of the trap while smiling inwardly at the cat caught in the trap below; just then the mouse Palita saw his two other enemies, an ichneumon on the ground and an owl on the tree, wanting to get him; Palita immediately realized that the cat, his third enemy in distress, was his only means of escape; he therefore offered the cat to cut off the cords of the net if the cat in return promised not to injure him when he moved near the cat to protect himself from the ichneumon and the owl; Palita wished that Lomaśa remained alive and expected a similar response from Lomaśa (तव जीवितम् इच्छामि त्वं ममे-च्छसि जीवितम् 12. 136. 59); the cat too knew that be by himself was almost at the end of his life (ताम् अवस्थाम् अवेक्-ष्यान्त्याम् 12. 136. 64) and hence spoke in conciliatory terms to the mouse; Lomaśa told the mouse that he had given up his pride and that he was Palita's devotee and pupil; he was prepared to carry out Palita's order and work in his interest; he requested Palita to do what would serve the purpose of both of them; Palita then suggested the following plan to Lomaśa: the mouse was to go very close to the cat and while he was in that condition the cat was to protect the mouse from the owl and the ichneumon; when the danger to the mouse from the two had passed, the mouse was to cut the cords of the net and free the cat; Lomaśa agreed to this plan and promised not only to be well-disposed towards Palita when he drew near, but also offered later to do, with his friends and relatives, things pleasing to Palita; the mouse then moved very close to the cat and slept on his chest; having seen that the ichneumon and the owl had returned to their respective homes Palita started to cut off the cords of the net slowly; Lomaśa tried to hasten him asking him not to be ungrateful; Lomaśa wanted Palita to finish the work before the Caṇḍāla (श्वपच) returned; Palita refused to hasten until he was sure that the Caṇḍāla was close by so that Lomaśa, when freed, would not pounce on the mouse but jump on the tree from the fear of the Caṇḍāla; Lomaśa again pleaded with Palita to be more quick in his work pointing out that good men did not act the way Palita was going about his work; Palita should not remember their past enmity and delay in freeing the cat; Palita assured Lomaśa that he had cut off most of the cords and deliberately left only one which he would bite off at the proper time; when the night ended and the Caṇḍāla was seen arriving, Lomaśa was frightened and asked Palita what he intended to do; Palita cut off the last cord and the freed Lomaśa jumped up the tree as was expected by Palita, and Palita himself entered his hole; when the disappointed Caṇḍāla went away, Lomaśa requested Palita not to misunderstand him if he, when he became free, jumped up the tree without conversing with Palita (अकृत्वा संविदं कांचित् सहसाहम् उपप्लुतः । कृतज्ञं कृतकल्याणं कच्चिन् मां नाभि-शङ्कसे 12. 136. 119); Lomaśa asked the mouse to trust him and come close to him as he wanted to honour Palita who had saved him; Lomaśa asked Palita to be his minister and instruct him like a father (अमात्यो मे भव प्राज्ञ पितेव हि प्रशाधि माम् 12. 136. 126); the counsel (मन्त्र) of the mouse and the strength (बल) of the cat together would win victories for them (12. 136. 127); but Palita pointed out to Lomaśa that he fell into the trap due to his thoughtlessness (चपलत्वात् 12. 136. 142); thoughtlessness does not help the person himself, how can it help others ?; Palita plainly told the cat that he wanted the mouse to move close to him because he was the food of the cat; Palita refused to go near Lomaśa when that was the cat's dinner time; Lomaśa made one more plea to Palita describing himself to be the knower of duties (धर्मज्ञ), apprecia-tive of the merits of others (गुणज्ञ), grate-ful for the good act (कृतज्ञ), and fond of friends (मित्रेषु वत्सल 12. 136. 179); if the mouse forsook the cat the latter would die; Palita, however, remained firm and advised Lomaśa to protect himself from the Caṇḍāla; hearing Caṇḍāla's name, the frightened Lomaśa quickly entered his hole, and Palita entered his 12. 136. 21-191.
लोहित: Lohita m.: A mythical serpent. One of the serpents who, without feeling fatigue, wait on god Varuṇa in his सभा; all serpents there marked with banner (पताकिन्) and round spots (मण्डलिन्), and were hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 8, 10, 11.

Lohita, Lohitoda, Lauhitya1 m.: Name of an ocean. A. Location: In the east (see My-thological event below) (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 17. 1. 33: लौहित्यम् उदयाचलप्रान्तस्थं समुद्रम्). B. Description: The abode of Varuṇa (वरुणालय) 3. 213. 28. C. Epic Event: When the Pāṇḍavas started on their great journey they first went to the Lau-hitya ocean (लौहित्यं सलिलार्णवम्) 17. 1. 31; there they saw god Agni and at his instance Arjuna returned his Gāṇḍīva bow and the two inexhaustible quivers to Varuṇa by throwing them into the water of the ocean 17. 1. 33-40. D. Mythological event: Before the birth of Skanda, Indra saw the Lohitoda ocean when he looked at the sun on the rising mountain 3. 213. 28, 26; the daughter of the Lohita ocean (लोह्त्-तस्योदधेः कन्या), cruel and drinking blood (क्रूरा लोहितभोजना), embraced the newly born Mahāsena (Skanda) and protected him like her son 3. 215. 22; the daughter of the Lohita ocean acted as the nurse of Skanda (धात्री स्कन्दस्य सा स्मृता); she is wor-shipped as Lohitāyani on the Kadamba tree (लोहितायनिर् इत्य् एवं कदम्बे सा हि पूज्-यते) 3. 219. 39; the seed of Rudra was poured in the womb of Umā; from there it fell out in five ways (तद् एवं पञ्चधापतत्): first (a part of) it fell on a mountain; the remaining in the Lohitoda ocean (लोहितोदे तु शुक्रशेषम् अवापतत्); a part fell in the rays of the sun, another part on earth, and the rest got stuck on trees 3. 220. 10-11.
लाङ्गल: Lāṅgala nt.: Plough used as a weapon by Balarāma. Hence Balarāma has epithets like लाङ्गलिन् 1. 213. 49; 9. 36. 36; 9. 38. 2; 9. 45. 93, 94; 9. 46. 23; 9. 54. 4; लाङ्गल-ध्वज 5. 3. 4.

Lāṅgala m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (लाङ्गलाः परवल्ल-काः) 6. 10. 55.
ललितिका: Lalitikā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। The तीर्थ of Śaṃtanu (शन्तनोस् तीर्-थम्) on the river Gaṅgā (?); described as the best तीर्थ (तीर्थम् उत्तमम्); by bath-ing there one does not meet with adversity (न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 82. 30.
लवेडिका: Laveḍikā f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as holy (पुण्या), resorted to by the holy (पुण्योपसेविता); by visiting it one gets the fruit of a Vājapeya; he rides in a विमान and is worshipped (विमानस्थश् च पूज्यते) 3. 82. 143.
लोकोद्धार: Lokoddhāra nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as an excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थ-वर) 3. 81. 37; famous in the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यविश्रुत) 3. 81. 36, 37; it was at this तीर्थ that Viṣṇu in the bygone days lifted the worlds (this explains the name of the तीर्थ) (लोका यत्रोद्धृताः पूर्वं विष्णुना) 3. 81. 36; by bathing there one lifts up his own kinsmen (लोकान् उद्धरते स्वकान्) 3. 81. 37.
लोलोद्धृतकरा: Loloddhṛtakarā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 30, 13 (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī).
लोहतारिणी: Lohatāriṇī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 17, 13 (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī).
लोहित्य: Lohitya1, Lauhitya2 m.: Name of the river Brahmaputra. A. Location: In the east (ययौ प्रा-चीं दिशं प्रति) 2. 26. 1; at the other end of the mountain Himavant, rising on the mountain of sunrise, flowing to the Vāriṣena (?) ocean (परार्धे हिमवतः सूर्योदय-गिरौ … । वारिषेणसमुद्रान्ते लोहित्यम् अभितश् च) 2. 48. 8. B. Description: Called a big river (महानदः) 13. 151. 16. C. Epic event: (1) Bhīmasena reached it in his expedition to the east before the Rāja-sūya (लौहित्यम् अगमद् बली); he collected there tributes of all sorts from all the Mleccha kings who lived in the islands of the ocean (Vāriṣeṇa ?) (लौहित्यम् अगमद् बली । स सर्वान् म्लेच्छनृपतीन् सागरद्वीपवासिनः । करम् आहारयाम् आस) 2. 27. 24-26; (2) The Kirāta kings who lived near the Lohitya river brought tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira at the time of his Rājasūya sacrifice; the tribute consisted of sandal-wood and other fragrant substances and heaps of skins, jewels and gold 2. 48. 9-10. D. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16, 2.

Lohitya2, Lauhitya3 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। The तीर्थ was established in the by-gone days by the grace of Rāma (Bhārgava); by visiting it one gets much gold (रामस्य च प्रसादेन तीर्थं राजन् कृतं पुरा । तल् लोहित्यं समासाद्य विन्द्याद् बहु सु-वर्णकम् ॥ ) 3. 83. 2; by visiting the Lau-hitya तीर्थ and by bathing there, according to the rites, at the conjunction of Urvaśī (?) and Kṛttikā a person who is well composed gets the fruit of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice (उर्वशी-कृत्तिकायोगे गत्वा यः सुसमाहितः । लौहित्ये विधिवत् स्नात्वा पुण्डरीकफलं लभेत्) 13. 26. 43 (For Nī. see p. 244. 2 under Kṛttikā).
लोहित्या: Lohityā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 34, 13 (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī).
लङ्का: Laṅkā f.: Name of the city of Rāvaṇa. A. Location: On the other side of the ocean (पारे महोदधेः) 3. 262. 33; in the valley of the Trikūṭa mountain on the other side of the ocean (पारे समुद्रस्य त्रिकूटगिरिकन्दरे) 3. 266. 55. B. History: Pitāmaha assigned Laṅkā, together with the Rākṣasas, to Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera) as the seat of his capital (पितामहस् तु … ददौ वैश्रवणस्य ह । … राजधानीनिवे-शं च लङ्कां रक्षगणान्विताम्) 3. 258. 15-16; Kubera, while living in Laṅkā gave three Rākṣasīs as servants to appease Viśra-vas, his father 3. 259. 3; Daśagrīva (Rāvaṇa), son of Viśravas, defeated Kubera in battle and drove him out of Laṅkā 3. 259. 32; Kubera left Laṅkā and entered Gandhamādana (हित्वा स भगवाई लङ्काम् आविशद् गन्धमादनम्) 3. 259. 33; Laṅkā then belonged to Rāvaṇa and he was its king (मम लङ्का पुरी नाम्ना) 3. 262. 33; 3. 266. 54; Rāvaṇa called king and resident of Laṅkā (राज्ञा लङ्कानिवासिना) 3. 263. 39; (लङ्कां भ्रातुर् निवेशनम्) 3. 261. 44. C. Description: Pleasing (रम्या) 3. 262. 33; naturally unassailable (प्रकृत्य-इव दुराधर्षा) 3. 268. 2; having strong ramparts with arched doorways (दृढ-प्राकारतोरणा) 3. 268. 2; its southern gate was unapprochable (दक्षिणं नगरद्वा-रं … दुरासदम्) 3. 268. 24; when besieged by Rāma, Rāvaṇa made arrangements (for the fortification) of the town as prescribed in the शास्त्र (रावणश् च विधिं चक्रे लङ्कायां शास्त्रनिर्मितम्) 3. 268. 2; the seven deep trenches around Laṅkā are des-cribed in 3. 268. 3-5; troops, both stationary and moving, consisting of many foot-sol-diers, elephants and horses, were stationed near all gates of the town (पुरद्वारेषु सर्वेषु गुल्माः स्थावरजङ्गमाः । बभू-वुः पत्तिबहुलाः प्रभूतगजवाजिनः) 3. 268. 6; called पूरी 3. 262. 33; 3. 264. 41; 3. 266. 68; 3. 268. 21; महापुरी 3. 266. 54; पुर 3. 268. 6; 3. 270. 29; 3. 271. 1; नगर 3. 268. 24. D. Rāmāyaṇa events: (1) Śūrpaṇakhā, when her nose and lips were cut off, went to Laṅkā the residence of her brother (ययौ … लङ्कां भ्रातुर् निवेशनम्) 3. 261. 44; (2) Rāvaṇa told Sītā that his town Laṅkā lay beyond the ocean (लङ्का पुरी … पारे महोदधेः) 3. 262. 33; (3) Gandharva Viśvāvasu told Rāma that Rāvaṇa had carried off Sītā to Laṅkā 3. 263. 39; (4) Rāvaṇa on reaching Laṅkā with Sītā placed her in an आश्रम-like dwelling near the Aśoka grove which was like Nandana (भवने नन्दनोपमे । अशोकवनिकाभ्याशे तापसा-श्रमसंनिभे) 3. 264. 41; (5) Sampāti told Hanūmant that Rāvaṇa to whom the big town Laṅkā belonged was known to him (रावणो विदितो मह्यं लङ्का चास्य महा-पुरी) 3. 266. 54; (6) Hanūmant burnt the town (Laṅkā) (ततो दग्ध्वा च तां पुरीम्) before returning to Rāma 3. 266. 68; Bhīma told Hanūmant that he (Hanū-mant) alone could destroy Laṅkā with its warriors and chariots (लङ्कां सयोधां सहवाहनाम्) 3. 149. 15; (7) When Rāma with his army crossed the ocean to reach Laṅkā, he asked the monkeys to destroy many large gardens there (लङ्कोद्यानान्य् अनेकशः । कपिभिर् भेदयाम् आस म-हान्ति च बहूनि च ॥ ) 3. 267. 51; Rāma is also reported to have burnt Laṅkā with his sharp arrows (दग्ध्वा लङ्कां शितैः शरैः) 3. 258. 3; (8) Aṅgada, as messen-ger of Rāma, reached the gate of Laṅkā (लङ्कायाः द्वारदेशम्) and entered it 3. 268. 7, 9; Aṅgada leapt over Laṅkā to return to Rāma (लङ्घयित्वा पुरीं लङ्काम्) 3. 268. 21; (9) Rāma shattered the ram-part of Laṅkā with the help of his fast monkey forces (भेदयाम् आस लङ्कायाः प्राकारं रघुनन्दनः) 3. 268. 23; (10) Lakṣmaṇa, with Vibhīṣaṇa and Jāmbavant, broke the unapproachable southern gate of the town (Laṅkā) (दक्षिणं नगरद्वा-रम्) 3. 268. 24; Laksmaṇa attacked Laṅkā with crores of monkeys 3. 268. 25; the ramparts of Laṅkā appeared tawny with monkeys moving on it (वानरैः … समन्तात् कपिलीकृतम्) 3. 268. 28; the monkeys broke the jewelled pillars and summits of watch-towers and threw on the town machines whose speed was checked and destroyed (by the summits of the towers) (बिभिदुस् ते मणिस्तम्भान् कर्णाट्टशिखराणि च । भग्नोन्मथितवेगानि यन्त्राणि च विचिक्षि-पुः) 3. 268. 29 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 284. 30: कर्णस् तिर्यग्यानं तेन प्रकारेण यत् पाषाणादिविस्तरेण क्रियते तत् तद् गृहविशे-षं कर्णाट्टम् इति वदन्ति); the monkeys threw the ‘hundred killer’ missiles together with wheels and stones (hurled) by हुडस् (?) inside Laṅkā (परिगृह्य शतघ्नीश् च सच-क्राः सहुडोपलाः । चिक्षिपुर् भुजवेगेन लङ्कामध्ये) 3. 268. 30; the monkeys chased the Rākṣasas who stood on the protective walls (of Laṅkā) (प्राकारस्थाश् च ये केचिन् निशाचरगणाः) 3. 268. 31; then the Rākṣasas attacked the monkeys and cleared the walls (कृतो निर्वानरो भूयः प्राकारो भीमदर्शनैः) 3. 268. 34; the arrows of Rāma reached as far as Laṅkā and killed the Rākṣasas in it (शरजालानि ववर्ष … । तानि लङ्कां समासाद्य जघ्नुस् तान् रजनीचरान्); Lakṣmaṇa too felled down the Rākṣasas standing at the fort-ress (of Laṅkā) (दुर्गस्थान् पातयाम् आस राक्षसान्) 3. 268. 38-39; there was much fighting in Laṅkā in which the targets were struck and victory was in view; then Rāma asked his armies to stop fighting (कृते विमर्दे लङ्कायाम् ल-ब्धलक्षो जयोत्तरः ॥ ) 3. 268. 40 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 284. 41: लब्धाः आयुधैः प्राप्ता लक्ष्या वध्या यस्मिन् । अवन्ध्य-प्रहार इति यावत् । जयोत्तरो जयोत्कर्ष-वान्); (11) At the fall of Dhūmrākṣa, the Rākṣasas, attacked by the monkeys, fled back to Laṅkā in fear 3. 270. 16; (12) Vajravega and Pramāthin, led by Kumbha-karṇa, came out of the town (Laṅkā) to fight with Rāma (तूर्णं निर्ययतुः पुरात्) 3. 270. 29; (ततो विनिर्याय पुरात् कुम्भ-कर्णः) 3. 271. 1; (13) The empty chariot of Indrajit, when he and his charioteer were killed by Lakṣmaṇa, was taken in-side Laṅkā by the horses (लङ्कां प्रवे-शयाम् आसुर् वाजिनस् तं रथं तदा) 3. 273. 25; (14) Rāvaṇa came out (of the city) in his chariot for his fight with Rāma (निर्ययौ रथम् आस्थाय) 3. 274. 1; (15) After killing Rāvaṇa, Rāma gave Laṅkā to Vibhīṣaṇa 3. 275. 5; (16) After making arrangements for the protection of Laṅkā Rāma, followed by Vibhīṣaṇa, crossed the ocean, along the same bridge, riding his Puṣpaka (रामः … विधाय रक्षां लङ्कायां विभीषणपुरस्-कृतः । संततार पुनस् तेन सेतुना मकरा-लयम् ॥ पुष्पकेण विमानेन) 3. 275. 50-52.
लडक: Laḍaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. On the second day of war, Laḍakas, along with Piśācas and other peoples, were stationed at the right wing of the Krauñ-cāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (मडका लडकाश् चैव  … एते जनपदा राजन् दक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 6. 46. 49-50.
ललाटाक्ष: Lalāṭākṣa m. (pl.): Name of a people. They came from different parts and gave tribute for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira large quantity of gold and silver, but were stopped at the gate (ललाटाक्षान् नानादिग्-भ्यः समागतान् । … द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारि-तान् । बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्मै हिरण्यं रजतं बहु ॥ ) 2. 47. 15-16.
ललित्थ: Lalittha m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Description: Honoured by heroes (शूरसंमत) 7. 66. 39; of firm determi-nation (दृढनिश्चय) 7. 16. 27. B. Epic events: (1) On the eleventh day of the war, at night, Lalitthas were among those who, led by Suśarman and his five bro-thers, vowed to kill Arjuna the next day; the mode of the oath in the presence of the fire in which offerings were given (ज्वल-नम् आदाय हुत्वा सर्वे पृथक् पृथक् 7. 16. 22; तस्मिन्न् अगनौ तदा चक्रुः प्रतिज्ञां दृढनिश्चयाः 7. 16. 27) and invoking severe penalty in case of failure to carry out the vow is described in 7. 16. 22-36; (2) On twelfth day, Arjuna afflicted Lahtthas with arrows; though getting killed, they continued to shower arrows of different kinds on Arjuna; as a result, both Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa could not be seen due to the shower of arrows; Lalitthas felt that they had hit the target and therefore they raised loud roar looking at each other; consider-ing that Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa were killed they joyfully waived their upper garments and sounded भेरिस्, मृदङ्गस् and conches in thousands (ततस् ते लब्धलक्ष्यत्वाद् अन्योन्यम् अभिचुक्रुशुः । हतौ कृष्णाव् इति प्रीता वासांस्य् आदुधुवुस् तदा । … सिंह-नादरवांश् चोग्रांश् चक्रिरे) 7. 18. 17-20; (3) On the fourteenth day, Lalitthas led by Jaya, Kṛtavarman and Droṇa tried to check the advance of Arjuna towards Jaya-dratha 7. 66. 38-43; in this context, Saṃjaya referred to Karṇa's former victory over Lalitthas in battle (कर्णेन विजिताः पूर्वं संग्रामे) 7. 66. 39 (reference to Karṇa's दिग्विजय before Duryodhana's Vaiṣṇava-yajña 3. 241. 29, 32; 3. App. I. 24. 28-34); (4) After the death of Karṇa, Saṃjaya while reporting to Dhṛtarāṣṭra mentioned Lalitthas among those who were killed by Arjuna in the war 8. 4. 46, 50.
लोह: Loha m. (pl.): Name of a people. Conquered by Arjuna in his expedition to the north (दिशं धनपतेर् इष्टाम् 2. 23. 9; 2. 24. 1) before the Rājasūya of Yudhi-ṣṭhira (लोहान् … व्यजयत् पाकशासनिः) 2. 24. 24.
लोहजङ्घ: Lohajaṅgha m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned by Duryodhana among those who at the time of Rājasūya, lying low, acted as dependents in the household of Yudhiṣṭhira (आवर्जिता इवाभान्ति निघ्नाश्  … । कारस्करा लोहजङ्घा … ) 2. 46. 21 [Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 50. 20: आवर्जिताः दासवद् वशगाः].
